items.excerpt: Pilgway released 3DCoat 2026 and the cut-down 3DCoatTextura 2026, headlined by a new GPU-accelerated node-based texturing system plus updates to sculpting, retopology and painting. Note: byline date only (no og/JSON-LD timestamp on CG Channel); no AI features in this release.
Autodesk's Arnold 7.5.3 adds new BSDF nodes for toon shading and an Accelerated Viewport mode for Maya, speeding up interactive look-dev. Byline date only (CG Channel exposes no og:published_time).

Sisir is a new free standalone hair-grooming tool that lets artists draw guides directly onto 3D characters and export the groom to Blender, Maya and UE5 -- a guide-based workflow that sidesteps each DCC's own hair system. Byline date only.

ArcBrush 1.5 moves to a color-managed 32-bit float image pipeline with Cryptomatte support and eleven new nodes, while explicitly reducing the tool's focus on AI and simplifying licensing to a $49 Pro tier -- a rare counter-move to the AI-first trend in texturing tools.

A new Blender add-on gives every object its own independent undo history, working across Object Mode, Sculpt, Paint, Pose and Animation editors -- a small but structural change to how non-linear 3D iteration feels.
StEM3 gives filmmakers a free, standardised toolkit to test, validate and trust an LED volume before the cameras roll -- calibration infrastructure for virtual-production stages.

At SIGGRAPH Nvidia laid out a 'hybrid AI' strategy for graphics: AI agents orchestrating classical rendering tools through new Omniverse libraries, aimed at controllable, physically accurate virtual worlds rather than one-shot generation.
HP's Z Captis 3D scanner gains an AI boost through integration with Adobe Substance 3D Sampler, tightening the loop from physical object capture to production-ready materials and assets.
ModuleWorks is bringing physics-based toolpath generation directly into Siemens NX CAM as Xcelerator plugins, pushing simulation-informed machining upstream into the design-to-manufacture handoff.
Builder.io argues designers should 'treat AI as your next user, not another feature' -- giving every agent a visible surface, state and personality instead of burying it behind a chat box.

Figma details a year of running security agents that guard code as it is written and review every pull request -- how the design-tool vendor itself operationalises always-on agents inside a product org.
An optical-illusion 'advert' featuring Kylie Jenner has become the sharpest piece of creative commentary on Meta's AI glasses -- a case study in art direction carrying a critique that copy cannot.
A practical breakdown of how the design handoff changes once a coding agent is the first reader: what 'AI-legible' specs, token naming and component contracts actually look like in a repo.
A 'trust test' of four questions every design tool -- Figma included -- should be able to answer about how it trains on and uses customer work, framed for design leads doing vendor due diligence.
With AI able to generate a plausible design portfolio end to end, the piece argues hiring signal has moved to the follow-up question -- the reasoning behind a decision, not the artifact.
An argument that the interface layers we keep adding -- now including AI-mediated ones -- have become a wall between people and the task they came to do.
Meta's new pro-AI ad campaign is conspicuously light on actual AI-generated craft -- a telling signal about where brands still believe human-made creative carries more trust.
Samsung unveiled more smart-glasses designs made with Gentle Monster and Warby Parker ahead of a fall release -- eyewear-first industrial design used to make an AI wearable socially wearable.

'Motion for people who are scared of motion software' -- a Figma Motion walkthrough where the Figma agent generates a starting animation the designer then refines on canvas, with no After Effects round-trip.
Gary Simon walks from ordinary photos of objects to a working Three.js 3D scene in minutes using AI image-to-3D reconstruction -- a concrete web-design pipeline rather than a demo reel.
'The Future of Creativity Is #NotGenerated' -- an Adobe x Parsons collaboration positioning human-made craft as the differentiator, from the company shipping the generative tools.
Short tutorial on animating loading states with the arc tool inside Figma Motion -- native timeline animation replacing a hand-off to After Effects or Lottie for a common UI pattern.

A behind-the-scenes video on Coca-Cola's new branding system and custom typeface -- a large-scale identity process shown end to end, useful as a contrast case to prompt-driven brand work. (Low AI hook; backfill only.)
